newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron drops 8.06 pct in midtrade.
newsitem.headline: Petron drops 8.06 pct in midtrade.

text.p: Philippine oil refiner Petron Corp shed 50 centavos, or 8.06 percent, to 5.70 pesos in midsession on Wednesday on continuing concerns over the effects of a weaker peso, brokers said.

"Oil companies may have to increase petroleum prices as a result of the peso's depreciation. Most of them are hedged so the impact will not be much. But there's negative sentiment on how the companies will cope," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities.
"It is also technical since Petron was one of those issues that rode the general buying last Friday," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities Inc.
The central bank allowed the peso to float in a wider range last Friday, triggering across-the-board buying in the stock market in anticipation of lower interest rates.
Garcia said he expected bargain-hunting on Petron when it goes down to 5.50 pesos.
Petron was one of the top five actively traded issue for the day.
